A higher-order composite box beam theory is developed to model rectangular beams with arbitrary wall thicknesses.
The theory is a three-dimensional model that approximates the elasticity solution, including both in-plane and out-of-plane warping deformations.
The model can accurately capture the transverse shear stresses through the thickness of each wall while satisfying stress-free boundary conditions on the inner and outer surfaces of the beam.
The aerodynamic loads are calculated using the classical blade element momentum theory, with analytical expressions for the lift and drag based on the blade planform.
The objective functions include the figure of merit in hover and the high-speed cruise propulsive efficiency.
Structural, aerodynamic, and aeroelastic stability criteria are imposed as constraints on the optimization problem.
The Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (K-S) function is used to formulate the multiobjective function problem, and a hybrid approximate analysis is used to reduce the computational effort.
The search direction is determined by the Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno algorithm.
The optimum results show significant improvements in the overall performance of the tilt-rotor blade compared to the baseline design.
The static results for beams with different wall thicknesses and aspect ratios show excellent agreement with available experimental data.
The dynamic results demonstrate the importance of including in-plane and out-of-plane warping deformations in the formulation.
Key challenges in tilt-rotor design include achieving a low disc loading in hover, managing high helical tip Mach numbers in high-speed cruise, and ensuring aeroelastic stability.
The higher-order composite box beam theory is a three-dimensional model that does not reduce the beam cross-sectional properties to one-dimensional parameters.
The use of numerical optimization techniques allows for the systematic exploration of the design trade-offs between conflicting requirements in tilt-rotor design.
The aeroelastic stability of the tilt-rotor blade is evaluated as a constraint in the optimization problem.
